notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT record: it stays inside the event's own inventory refs, is shorter than the prophet story that also tells the event, and refers to that story only in general words. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims; passages from several surahs are grouped by theme and surah order is not time order. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The one who speaks in the passage asked his Lord to show him how He gives life to the dead.
God asked whether he did not believe, and he answered yes, but that his heart might be at ease.
God told him to take four of the birds and to incline them to himself, the Arabic being read in more than one way.
Then he was to place a part of them on every mountain.
Then he was to call them, and they would come to him hastening.
God told him to know that God is Almighty and Wise.

chapters.summary_md: The one who speaks in the passage asked his Lord to show him how He gives life to the dead [c1]. God told him to take four birds and to call them, and they would come to him hastening [c3][c5].
chapters.body_md:
The one who speaks in the passage asked his Lord to show him how He gives life to the dead [c1]. God asked whether he did not believe, and he answered yes, but that his heart might be at ease [c2].

God told him to take four of the birds and to incline them to himself [c3]. Then he was to place a part of them on every mountain [c4], and then to call them, and they would come to him hastening [c5]. God told him to know that God is Almighty and Wise [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The passage is a short exchange in which a request [c1] is met by a question and an answer [c2], and then by an instruction in steps [c3][c4][c5]. The instruction ends with a reminder of God's might and wisdom [c6]. The Arabic of the first step, rendered 'incline them to yourself', is read in more than one way [c3].
chapters.kids_md: A servant of God asked Him to show how He gives life to the dead [c1]. God told him to take four birds and to call them, and they would come to him [c3][c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the speaker says belief and a heart at ease are not the same thing, and God does not rebuke the request [c2]. Another is that the passage ends by naming God as Almighty and Wise [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which birds, where, or when; the verse says only four of the birds.
- The Arabic phrase in the first step is read in more than one way (to incline them to yourself, or to cut them up); the verse does not decide, and a scholar should word it.
- Not established: what happened to the birds after the call beyond that they come hastening; the verse does not describe it.
- Not established: what it means that the parts were placed on every mountain, or how many mountains.
- The verse does not say what prompted the request.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this request and the birds. None is used in this draft.
The event is also told inside the longer story of the same prophet (content/stories/ibrahim.draft.json); this record is a shorter account that refers to it only in general words.

The text of this event never names its speaker in the draft because the spelling of the name at 2:260 is not matched by the name anchor in the validator fixtures (a validator limitation, not a Quranic point); the passage itself names him in its first words.
The reading of the Arabic verb translated 'incline them to yourself' (the cutting up of the birds, or only turning them toward him) is disputed among interpreters; the draft keeps both.
The chapters group repeated passages by theme. The Quran does not give a chronology across the surahs, so the order of the chapters is a reading order only.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
